Making Sense Of The Semiconductor Jitters

Udith Sikand

Gavekal Research | 29 Jul 2026

The jitters in global chip stocks seen in recent weeks show few signs of abating (see The Hardware Sell-Off). The Bloomberg global semiconductor index fell -7% on Tuesday and is now down -25% since peaking on June 22. South Korea’s memory champions were especially hard hit, triggering a wave of selling across Asian markets before it spread to Europe and the US and continued in Asian trading on Wednesday.The benign take of this repricing is that, after a strong run-up in recent months, markets are simply consolidating as momentum-chasing investors have overextended themselves. On this view, the recent sell-off is a buy-the-dip opportunity, as semiconductor valuations remain undemanding given the still-favorable earnings momentum.
